title: Choose the expression of "Inside the machine"
question: Your world is pinned. The roll picked how to express it: the datasheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Datasheet and the Board
options.lineage: IC datasheets, pinout diagrams, and the PCB the part sits on
options.thesis: You read the part's datasheet, then you walk inside the part.
materials: cool datasheet paper and black ink
matte-black solder mask, copper traces, white silkscreen
options.viewport: Title Screen is a datasheet cover: part number LA-1 'Luan Afonso', and a chip pinout where NEW GAME and SKIP are pins; the selected pin's trace runs copper. NEW GAME dives into the chip and the game is the board inside: black solder-mask walls, silkscreen labels, insect Bugs. Exhibit Panel is a datasheet page pulled over the game; the Skip View is the full datasheet.
options.risk: Paper outside, board inside: two materials must read as one system, or it feels like two sites.

raised.raise: Traceability: each Exhibit gets a reference designator (U1 project, J1 contact, R1 skill, Q1 job) that is the same on the wall, in the Exhibit Panel, and in the Skip View.
Discrete states: select, press, and fix are step changes, not soft glows; a fixed Bug leaves a silkscreen 'patched' mark.
Copper means live: copper only marks the selected item and traces carrying signal; everything else is ink, paper, or board.
Pixel honesty: pixel type and pixel art only at whole-pixel sizes.
Declared ornament tiers: traces and silkscreen ornament drop in two declared steps at narrow widths; content never shrinks.

options.label: The Circuit Board
options.thesis: Everything is the board: menus, panels, and walls are solder mask and copper.
options.viewport: Title Screen is a top-down board; your name is silkscreen; menu items are pads joined by traces.
options.risk: The literal reading of the brief and the most familiar one; it can drift toward a generic 'tech' wallpaper.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: The portfolio as an old black-and-white desktop: windows, dithers, marching ants.
options.viewport: A dithered desktop; NEW GAME and SKIP are icons; the Exhibit Panel is a window.
options.case: Developers know it by heart; it is the computer's face, not its inside, so it loses on the brief.
options.risk: Reads as a retro OS homage instead of 'inside the machine'.

options.label: Jacquard Brocade
options.thesis: Binary choices woven into one picture.
options.viewport: Loom rows that weave the name.
options.case: Beautiful, but visitors do not read a loom as a developer.

options.label: Forge Scale Shower
options.thesis: Each blow visibly changes the metal.
options.case: Too violent for harmless Bugs; no developer identity.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: A row of needles reads the room.
options.case: An audio world, not a code world.

options.label: Emigre Bitmap Specimen
options.case: A type poster, not a place to walk.

options.label: Info-noise Sleeve
options.viewport: One huge word through the noise.
options.case: Too loud for recruiters reading a portfolio.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer-portfolio game skin: terminal font, one accent, clean panels.
canonCard.viewport: Centered name, two menu items, a clean status bar in game.
canonCard.risk: Clean, but forgettable next to other dev portfolios.
